card.name: Words just before dose adjustment
card.fires_on: Words in drug-interaction text where a dose change is about to be mentioned, such as requirements, dosage, lower or titrate, often after insulin, warfarin or lithium.

modes.label: Insulin or drug requirements
modes.description: The word requirements or dosage right after insulin or an antidiabetic drug, where a change in need is described.
modes.example: may decrease blood glucose and insulin<< requirements>> ( 7.1 ). • Oral

modes.label: Titrate and monitor wording
modes.description: Start or inside of titrate, or words like be and concentrations, in advice to monitor and change a drug.
modes.example: Succinylcholine chloride injection must be<< tit>>rated to effect by or under supervision of

modes.label: Dosage before adjustment
modes.description: The word dosage or lower directly before adjustment of another drug is mentioned.
modes.example: Antidiabetic drugs (oral agents and insulin) -<< dosage>> adjustment of the antidiabetic drug may

card.writes: It promotes the word adjust and its variants, so the next word is likely to be about adjusting a dose.
card.plain: It fires where a label is about to say a dose may need to be adjusted because of another drug.
